name: Graphite
tagline: Veteran metrics stack: Carbon ingestion, Whisper files and the render API that shaped modern dashboards.
description: Graphite is the open-source metrics stack, first released by Orbitz in 2008, that popularised dotted metric names, the plaintext "path value timestamp" protocol and the function-chaining render API Grafana was originally built around. Carbon daemons receive metrics, Whisper fixed-size files store them with pre-declared retention and rollups, and graphite-web serves the render and find APIs. It is easy to reason about but scales only by manual sharding with carbon-relay, and its tag support arrived late, so most new deployments pick a Prometheus-compatible system and keep the Graphite protocol only for legacy emitters. Volunteers still merge fixes, but there has been no tagged release since 2022.
statusNote: Volunteer-maintained; last tagged release 1.1.10 (May 2022), with recent commits limited to fixes and dependency updates.

pricing.notes: Hosted Graphite-compatible services exist, e.g. Grafana Cloud.

scale.notes: Scale by sharding Whisper files across hosts with carbon-relay consistent hashing.

strengths: Dead-simple plaintext protocol supported by almost every metrics library and StatsD
Predictable disk usage: Whisper files are preallocated per retention policy
Rich library of render functions for transforming series
Mature, well understood and supported in Grafana
weaknesses: Disk I/O heavy: one file per metric and per-point writes
Clustering is manual sharding with no automatic rebalancing
Hierarchical names make label-style slicing awkward even with tags
